summary.headline: Repco Home Finance Q1 FY27: disbursements Rs.843 Cr (vs Rs.829 Cr), AUM Rs.15,990 Cr up 8.9% YoY; management flags spread compression of up to 10bps.
summary.overview: Sanctions rose to Rs.938 Cr from Rs.907 Cr in FY26 and disbursements edged up to Rs.843 Cr from Rs.829 Cr, with management attributing the soft quarter to April-May transfers and promotions. Net profit rose to Rs.114 Cr from Rs.108 Cr and NII to Rs.216 Cr from Rs.207 Cr, while GNPA was Rs.427 Cr (2.7%) versus Rs.405 Cr (2.6%) in the prior quarter. Management guided to a more aggressive disbursement stance, accepting a possible 10-12bps spread decline to fund growth and curb BT-outs. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs.5,000 Cr disbursements, 13-14% AUM growth and a Rs.40 Cr NPA reduction.

segments.name: Housing loans vs home equity (non-HL)
segments.commentary: Home loans are 71% of the book and non-HL home equity loans 29% as of June 2026. Non-salaried borrowers are 53.5% of exposure and salaried 46.5%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Tamil Nadu accounts for about 57% of the book. Management is now prioritising southern non-TN states (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka), with Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Gujarat and MP in the pipeline.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: Rs.5,000 Cr disbursements, 13-14% AUM growth, and Rs.40 Cr NPA reduction.
Q2 FY27 disbursement target of Rs.1,200-1,250 Cr; management says June, July and early August trends are on track.
Gross NPA to be brought back to about Rs.405 Cr in Q2 and to around Rs.400 Cr by September end; target of less than 2% GNPA by March 2027.
Spread may fall by 10-12bps, at most 10bps, in the next quarter, then broadly stable, as the company sacrifices yield to drive disbursements and curb BT-outs.
Cost of funds expected to stay stable at around 8.3%, supported by the Rs.600 Cr NHB refinance line (Rs.106 Cr drawn in early August, with Rs.100 Cr later referenced as undertaken).
Plans to open 12-13 more branches in FY27, mainly in AP, Telangana, Karnataka and western states.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 242 branches, including about 32 satellite centres; no new branches opened in Q1 FY27.
Plan to add 12-13 branches in FY27, focused on Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and western India.
IT transformation completed in two phases, including mobile apps and API integrations with Perfios, CERSAI and CIBIL to shorten sanction turnaround.
Operating model verticalised: separate vertical for recoveries and SARFAESI, a separate sales vertical, DSAs, DSTs and connectors added.
demand_pricing: Customer rates start at 8.75% with an average of about 10.5% on housing loans; management says pricing is risk-based on 16-17 parameters and PSU-bank rates are not viable at its cost of borrowing.
Q1 disbursement shortfall attributed to April-May transfers and promotions; management says June was good and July and August are running ahead.
BT-outs rose in Q1 versus Q4. Management is retaining good-track-record borrowers with rate concessions and a new incentive scheme for staff.
Competition is intensifying from other HFCs and NBFCs; management says it has grown through competition for 25 years.
Sourcing focus moved partly from DSAs to other channels, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why is customer lending rate high versus banks, and why is the company not diversifying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rate depends on cost of borrowing (about 8.3-8.35%) and risk profile, and PSU-rate lending is not viable. It has no current plan to diversify beyond housing finance, and an HFC licence limits it to housing and mortgage loans.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q1 disbursement affected by cheque issues, and is there a Q1 backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said month-end disbursements of about Rs.35-40 Cr roll over each month as a normal cycle; June's figure carries the operational impact and any backlog will be made up in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Are June and July run-rates back to normal, and is the Rs.1,200 Cr Q2 target credible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June was good, July was better and August is expected to exceed that, and the MD said he was confident of Rs.1,200 Cr, while declining to give exact figures citing price-sensitive policy.

qa_highlights.question: Have pricing or customer policies changed, and what is driving the higher runoff?
qa_highlights.answer: No major policy change; sourcing focus shifted and some rate concessions were given to retain customers. Higher BT-outs reflect competitors targeting the company's visibility from more aggressive marketing.

qa_highlights.question: Is asset quality deterioration business as usual, and can recoveries outpace provisions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the NPA uptick to transfers and promotions. Soft NPAs (April 2025-June 2026 slippages, about 1,000-1,100 cases, 40-45 per RVM) are targeted for at least 50% reduction, worth Rs.70-75 Cr, and chronic NPAs are being pursued via SARFAESI.

qa_highlights.question: How much spread compression and what does it do to ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is 3.44% with cost of funds at 8.31%, and ROA around 2.9%. Spread may fall 10-12bps (maximum 10bps) next quarter, then stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company recognising interest and disbursement only on cheque encashment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said AUM and disbursement are booked only after encashment, and management said this has been the practice for three to four quarters.
